answer: Each agent identity must bond scarce tokens before it can submit work, and a beacon randomly assigns bonded identities to a trellis of review groups. Reviewers stake their own bonds on verdicts; when independent evidence exposes a fabricated agent, its bond is slashed and part of the loss goes to reporters. The random assignment prevents one operator from reliably packing a single group, while the bond makes creating many disposable identities costly. A saffron-colored badge may mark status, but it cannot replace the economic stake.
